summary: Define entities at first mention and re-enter later; part-of only (no inverse :part), for any part/format argument; enforce ARG0-only rolesets (checklist); no node for a connective linking to an earlier sentence; stricter :same-event; narrative change defaults to :overlap; trailing clause attaches to the creation verb's own argument. Trimmed intro/header text to stay under the limit.

edits.old:
Take the time this needs:

- Read the guidelines below carefully before you start, and go back to them for every decision you are
  not sure of: the concept and its sense, the numbered and non-core roles, abstract concepts and named
  entities, aspect, modal strength, polarity, and the temporal, modal and coreference relations.
- Follow the examples: when a sentence has a construction an example shows, annotate it the way the
  example does.
- Do not guess when you can check: the answer to almost every question is in the guidelines above and
  their examples; look it up there rather than answer from memory.
edits.new:
Take the time this needs:

- Read the guidelines below first and look up every decision you are unsure of; annotate a construction an example shows the way the example does.

edits.old:
A short version of the UMR 0.9 specification (`umr_guidelines.md` in this folder, umr4nlp/umr-guidelines),
for annotating Chinese and English at Stage 1 (numbered PropBank roles). It keeps what an annotator needs for
most sentences and leaves out the typological material, the fine-grained lattices, the field-linguistics
sections and most of the examples. Where the full guideline uses the older short names (`AUTH`, `DCT`,
`FullAff`, `:modstr`, `:ref-person`, `Performance`), this version uses the names of the UMR release data
(`author`, `document-creation-time`, `full-affirmative`, `:modal-strength`, `:refer-person`, `performance`).
edits.new: UMR 0.9, abridged, for Chinese and English at Stage 1 (numbered PropBank roles), with the names of the UMR release data.

(re-entrancy: `:ARG0 s3p` above). Write the full node (name, appositive, `:part-of`) at the entity's first mention in word order, even inside a subordinate clause below the root; every later mention, also inside a relative clause, is a re-entrancy.

edits.old: Copy the numbers from the roleset's role list every time.
edits.new: Copy the numbers from the roleset's role list every time. If the roleset lists only `:ARG0`, the single participant is `:ARG0` even when it looks like a patient (it starts, ceases, is founded, appears).

edits.old: - Every Chinese predicate uses the sense and numbered roles of its own PropBank roleset.
edits.new: - Every Chinese predicate uses the sense and numbered roles of its own PropBank roleset (`:ARG1` only if the roleset has one).

edits.anchor: *but* (但是, 却, 然而, 不过) `but-91`;
edits.text: a sentence-initial connective whose first conjunct is in an earlier sentence gets no node and no modal triple (the main verb is the root);

edits.old: When a format, layout or section noun (版面, edition, section) is what is created or changed for a publication, that noun is the argument and the publication is its `:part-of`.
edits.new: When a format, layout or section noun (版面, edition, section) of a publication is an argument of any verb, that noun is the argument and the publication is its `:part-of`. Never write the inverse `:part` on the whole.

edits.old: It attaches under that object as `:ARGn-of`
edits.new: It attaches under that object (the creation verb's own argument, not its `:part-of` whole) as `:ARGn-of`

edits.old: takes that earlier event as its reference time (`:overlap` or `:after`).
edits.new: takes that earlier event as its reference time with `:overlap` (`:after` only with an explicit later-sequence word).
(the same act mentioned again, same arguments in the same roles; not a retelling with another object or agent, or a part instead of the whole).
